items.title: Every enterprise has that one service nobody wants to upgrade
items.text:
• Still on Java 8
  • Half its dependencies are past end-of-life
  • The person who understood the build left two years ago
  • The upgrade ticket is old enough to have an anniversary

Now multiply that by hundreds of repositories.

items.title: Why it never gets prioritized
items.text:
The business sees

  • No new feature
  • No visible change for customers
  • "Fixes some vulnerabilities"

Engineering sees

  • Weeks of careful work
  • A risky, poorly tested build
  • A growing pile of CVEs

It sounds like a chore, so it loses to the roadmap every time.

items.title: What changed
items.text:
Frontier models like Claude Mythos made finding vulnerabilities fast and cheap. In Anthropic's Project Glasswing, partners found:

10,000+ high and critical issues, in a single month

The bottleneck was not detection. It was verifying and shipping the patches.

The new reality

Finding the holes is fast now. Fixing them is the slow part.

If defenders find flaws at that pace, attackers will too. When a patch lands, how fast you can apply it depends on how current your stack is:

flowchart LR
    CVE([🚨 Vulnerability disclosed]) --> PATCH[📦 Patched library released]
    PATCH --> Q{Is your stack current?}
    Q -- Yes --> FAST[Bump version<br/>run tests<br/>ship]
    Q -- "No, 3 majors behind" --> SLOW[Forced migration<br/>you postponed for years]
    FAST --> SAFE([✅ Patched in days])
    SLOW --> RISK([⚠️ Exposed for weeks or months])

    classDef good fill:#1f6f43,stroke:#2ea043,color:#fff
    classDef bad fill:#7a1f1f,stroke:#f85149,color:#fff
    class FAST,SAFE good
    class SLOW,RISK bad

Staying current isn't hygiene anymore. It's how fast you can respond when it matters.

Upgrading one app isn't hard. Doing it consistently, safely and repeatedly across a portfolio is, and it eats senior engineering time.

02 · How it works

items.title: A controlled workflow, not one giant prompt
items.text:
Not a single prompt that says "upgrade my app". Each agent has one job, and a human approves each report before the next phase starts.

  • Discover

    Collects a factual inventory of dependencies, versions, vulnerabilities and test coverage. Changes nothing.

  • Determine

    Plans the upgrade from that evidence, and scores whether your tests are strong enough to trust it.

  • Test

    Strengthens weak tests, round by round on its own branch, before anything is upgraded.

  • Code

    Upgrades Java, Spring Boot and dependencies, one verified commit at a time.

The Orchestrator ties the phases together, persists state between them and pauses for your approval. Nothing is merged or pushed: the result is a branch for your team to review.

03 · Why this approach

items.title: Tools do the work. The model does the thinking.
items.text:
Most of the pipeline is deterministic. Anything with a known right answer is handled by proven tools, not worked out by the model each time. The LLM reasons only where there is a real need.

Deterministic

Deterministic

Judgment

  • Fewer tokens, lower cost

    Reasoning is spent on judgment, not on work a tool already does reliably.

  • Reproducible

    Same input, same output. Scans, scores and rewrites don't vary between runs.

  • Reviewable

    Plans are approved before code changes. Changes land as small, verified commits.

  • Fast

    Scans run in parallel and the analysis scripts finish in seconds.

The model thinks only where there is a real need. Fewer tokens, lower cost, and results you can reproduce.

items.title: OpenRewrite
items.text: Recipes rewrite the Java code for the target Java and Spring Boot versions. The same migration, applied the same way, every time.

items.title: Bash and Python scripts
items.text: Run the Maven scans, reconcile dependencies and plugins, compute the testability score, track state and verify every build.

items.title: Claude
items.text: Writes the plan from the reports, writes tests that assert real behaviour, and summarises each report for you to approve.

items.title: What it unlocks
items.text:
Before After Every upgrade done differently Same playbook every time Long gap between patch released and patch deployed Shorter exposure window Surprises discovered in the diff Plans reviewed before code changes Test gaps found in production Test gaps found up front "Why did we change this?" Audit trail of what changed and why Seniors hand-editing pom.xml Seniors reviewing changes An LLM reasoning through every step Tokens spent only on judgment

What it is not

Not a magic "modernize everything" button. Humans still approve the plan and review the PRs. The goal is to take the repetitive, error-prone work off people's plates, not the judgment.

items.title: Code

The builder of the pipeline. It upgrades Java, Spring Boot and dependencies one verified commit at a time, on a branch you review and merge.

items.title: What this is
items.text: The code phase is the only phase that changes production code. coding-agent upgrades Java and Spring Boot to the versions you choose using OpenRewrite, refreshes the dependency facts against the upgraded build, removes <version> elements that an imported BOM already manages, and bumps outdated dependency, plugin and BOM versions. Every change is verified with a Maven build and test run before it is committed, one commit per change, on a separate branch. The phase ends with a final full build and modernization-summary-report.md.

items.title: Purpose
items.text: This is where the approved plan becomes code. Small, separately verified commits mean a reviewer can follow the upgrade step by step, and revert or cherry-pick any single change. "Verified" means the project builds and its tests run and pass after each change. It does not guarantee identical behaviour in production, which is why the branch is left for a person to review and merge.

items.title: Target version selection
items.text:
Just before the code phase starts for the first time, the orchestrator asks you which Java and Spring Boot versions to upgrade to. It offers MODERNIZATION_TARGET_JAVA_VERSION and MODERNIZATION_TARGET_SPRING_BOOT_VERSION as defaults and names the versions the upgrade skill has recipes for. Your answer is stored in .modernization/state.json as gates.target_java_version and gates.target_spring_boot_version. The orchestrator also records MODERNIZATION_CURRENT_JAVA_VERSION as gates.current_java_version, without asking. The Java version you choose must not be newer than the target JDK in MODERNIZATION_TARGET_JAVA_HOME.

The question is asked by the orchestrator because an agent cannot ask you anything. It is asked once per run: retries and resumed sessions reuse the stored answer.

Supported targets Default offered Java 17, 21, 25 25 Spring Boot 3.5, 4.1 4.1

Your answer wins over the plan

modernization-plan.md always states "Java 21 and Spring Boot 4.1 or later" as fixed template text. The code phase applies only the versions you choose here. Spring Boot 4.1 has no recipe yet, so pre-flight rejects it and names the versions that are available.

items.title: Which JDK builds what
items.text:
The pipeline uses two JDKs, both set in .claude/settings.json:

  • The current JDK (MODERNIZATION_CURRENT_JAVA_VERSION and MODERNIZATION_CURRENT_JAVA_HOME) is the one your project builds on today. Discover, test and the OpenRewrite migration itself run on it, because they all build the code before it is upgraded.
  • The target JDK (MODERNIZATION_TARGET_JAVA_VERSION and MODERNIZATION_TARGET_JAVA_HOME) is the one you upgrade to. Every build after the migration runs on it.

Each script sets JAVA_HOME for its own run only. Your shell, sdk default and the project's .sdkmanrc are left alone, so you never switch JDKs by hand.

items.title: Pre-flight checks
items.text:
Nothing is touched until both halves pass. If either fails, the agent records error.step: preflight and stops without creating a worktree.

Pipeline artifacts. The run is in CODING_RUNNING; the determine phase is approved; modernization-plan.md, dependency-report.md, plugin-report.md and testability-report.md exist in .modernization/determine/; discover's effective-pom, version-updates and bom-catalog folders exist; and the repository is a git work tree.

Environment. upgrade-java-spring-boot/scripts/pre-flight.sh checks:

  1. Both JDKs exist. For the current and the target JDK, both settings must be set, the home folder must contain bin/java, and that java must report the version you declared. If either JDK fails, pre-flight prints the reason for each one and stops immediately, without running the checks below.
  2. A recipe exists for each requested version. The list of supported versions is read from the recipe folders on disk, so it cannot drift from what is actually available.
  3. The JDKs fit the upgrade. The target JDK must be at least the Java version you chose ("at least", not "equal": building for Java 21 on JDK 25 is fine). After switching to the current JDK, mvn -v must report it. This catches a ~/.mavenrc that overrides JAVA_HOME.
  4. Project structure: root POM present, any requested module declared, POM well-formed.

Checks 2 to 4 report every problem rather than stopping at the first.

items.title: What it does
items.text:
After pre-flight, the agent upgrades the code in a separate worktree, one stage at a time. Each change is verified with a Maven build and test run before it is committed.

flowchart TD
    PF["0. Pre-flight"] --> WT["1. Resume or create worktree"]
    WT --> A["Stage A: Java and Spring Boot upgrade<br/>(OpenRewrite → full build → commit)"]
    A --> B["Stage B: Refresh dependency facts<br/>→ upgrade-worklist.csv"]
    B --> C["Stage C: Drop BOM-redundant versions<br/>(all → full build → one commit)"]
    C --> DL
    subgraph DL["Stage D: Bump outdated versions (per row)"]
        D1["Edit pom.xml"] --> D2["Quick build"]
        D2 -- "green" --> D3["Commit, mark applied"]
        D2 -- "red" --> D4["Revert, mark failed"]
    end
    DL --> E["Stage E: Final full build<br/>→ change log, build report, summary"]
    E --> DONE(["Done"])
Stage What it does Commits A OpenRewrite migration to the target Java and Spring Boot versions One, if anything changed B Re-checks dependency facts against the upgraded build and writes the worklist None C Removes <version> elements that an imported BOM already manages One for the batch D Bumps outdated versions One per bump, by default E Final full build, then the change log, build report and summary None

Empty stages are normal. A project already at the target version has nothing for stage A; a project already relying on BOM-managed versions has nothing for stage C. Both are recorded as completed, not treated as failures, and no empty commit is made.

items.title: Step 1: Resume or create the worktree
items.text:
On a fresh run the agent creates .modernization/code/state.json and the worktree:

git worktree add .modernization/code/worktree -b modernization/coding-agent-<run_id> <base-ref>

The base is the test branch when one is recorded. If .modernization/test/state.json has outputs.worktree_branch, the code branch starts from it, so the upgrade is verified against the improved tests. Otherwise it starts from HEAD. The choice is stored as outputs.base_ref.

If the worktree already exists, the agent reuses it, first discarding any uncommitted changes. Every verified change is already committed, so anything uncommitted is unverified work from an interrupted session. It then resumes at the first stage not marked completed.

items.title: Stage A: Java and Spring Boot upgrade
items.text:
apply-recipes.sh --workdir .modernization/code/worktree \
  --output-dir .modernization/code/upgrade-java-spring-boot \
  --java-version <v> --spring-boot-version <v>
build-verify.sh .modernization/code/worktree .modernization/code/build-verify/stage-a --jdk target

apply-recipes.sh runs on the current JDK. From here on, every build-verify.sh call in the phase uses --jdk target, and so does the inventory re-run in stage B.

apply-recipes.sh combines the recipe files for the requested versions into one rewrite.yml and runs mvn rewrite:run, with a one-hour timeout by default. Its status line reports how many files changed.

  • No files changed: the project is already at the target. Recorded, no commit.
  • Build green: committed. There is no scope check here, because an OpenRewrite migration is expected to change both production and test source.
  • Build red: the agent reads the extracted errors, repairs the source and re-verifies, within a limited budget. If it cannot repair it, the phase fails with step: java_spring_upgrade.

Stage A is committed before stage B starts, so the most expensive work survives a later failure.

Output: one commit; upgrade-java-spring-boot/rewrite.yml, logs/rewrite.log, and rewrite-errors.txt on failure

items.title: Stage B: Refresh dependency facts
items.text:
The determine phase's dependency report was written before the upgrade. The new Spring Boot parent or BOM now manages versions it did not before, and some recommended bumps may already have been applied by OpenRewrite. So the agent re-runs the relevant scripts against the worktree (not the phases: no state changes and no approval gates are reopened):

  1. inventory-orchestrator.sh --only effective-pom,version-updates in the worktree (deliberately without --force, which would also re-run the slow coverage and CVE tasks)
  2. generate-dependency-report.sh in the worktree, copied to .modernization/code/dependency-report.md
  3. plan-upgrades.sh, which runs versions:display-property-updates and combines it with the refreshed report to produce the worklist

Why property updates matter. Most POMs set versions through properties (<version>${kotlin.version}</version>), and one property can move several dependencies at once. The report alone also cannot see past an imported BOM: dozens of rows can look "managed by spring-boot-dependencies" when that BOM's own version is a property in your root POM. Property updates make those reachable. Pre-releases (alpha, beta, milestone, release candidate, snapshot) are excluded.

The agent marks this stage completed before moving on and never re-runs it once bumps have started, because regenerating the worklist would reset every applied row to pending and lose the record of what already landed.

Output: upgrade-worklist.csv, refreshed dependency-report.md

The worklist has one row per planned edit:

Column Meaning stage C (remove a redundant version) or D (bump) action drop-version, bump-version or none edit_kind property or version: which kind of edit to apply edit_pom, locator Which POM, and which property or groupId:artifactId current_version, target_version From and to status pending, applied, failed, deferred, covered or skipped commit, note The commit that applied it, or why it failed

covered means the row cannot be edited directly but moves anyway because the BOM that manages it is being bumped. Recording this keeps the change log honest about why a dependency changed.

items.title: Stage C: Drop BOM-redundant versions
items.text:
All drop-version rows are one logical change, so the agent removes them all, runs one full build, checks that only pom.xml files changed, and makes one commit.

If the build fails, it reverts them all, re-applies them one at a time with quick builds, and marks the ones that break the build as failed. A removal that breaks the build means the report's "managed by this BOM" inference was wrong for that row, which is useful to know. This is not a phase failure.

Output: one commit; worklist rows applied or failed

items.title: Stage D: Bump outdated versions
items.text:
For each pending stage=D row, by default one at a time:

  1. Edit the POM: set-property for a property, set-version for a literal version.
  2. Run a quick build (build-verify.sh --quick, without clean).
  3. Green: check that only pom.xml files changed, commit, mark the row applied with the commit.
  4. Red: revert that POM, mark the row failed with the first error line, move on.
  5. Record progress in steps.dependency_bumps.progress.

A failed bump is never a phase failure. One dependency that cannot be upgraded must not discard the ones that could.

apply-pom-edit.sh changes at most one line and leaves every other byte of the file as it was, so each commit's diff shows exactly the change and nothing else. It refuses to set a literal version on a dependency whose version is a property, and names the property to edit instead. It writes to a temporary file and renames it, so an interrupted edit cannot leave a broken POM.

With MODERNIZATION_CODING_BUMP_BATCH_SIZE above 1, that many bumps are applied per build; if the build fails, the batch is reverted and re-applied one at a time. With MODERNIZATION_CODING_MAX_BUMPS above 0, rows beyond the limit are marked deferred, not lost. Rows marked covered need no action.

Output: one commit per applied bump; worklist rows updated as each finishes

items.title: Stage E: Final verification and reports
items.text:
1. One full build (clean install, no --quick). Nothing is reported as finished on quick builds alone. A red final build means an interaction the quick builds hid: the agent tries to repair it, and if it cannot, the phase fails with step: final_verify and no success report is written.
  2. Writes the reports below.
  3. Sets status: completed and records the outcome in outputs.

Output:

File Contents .modernization/code/change-log.md Stage A summary (versions before and after, recipes, files changed, commit); stage C and D tables; a "Deferred and failed" section with reasons, so nothing silently disappears .modernization/code/build-report.md One row per build: stage, quick or full, status, duration, test counts. This is the evidence behind "every commit is green" .modernization/modernization-summary-report.md The page to read first. Outcome (versions before and after, final build, counts); links to every phase's report; gains realized compared with the plan; what is left; where to see the changes and the branch base

items.title: What "verified green" guarantees
items.text:
build-verify.sh runs the build and test suite, writes all Maven output to a log, and reports one status line plus build-summary.json. Its exit codes:

Exit Meaning 0 Build succeeded and the test checks below passed 1 Build failed; see build-errors.txt 3 Build succeeded but the tests did not really run 124 Timed out (default one hour) 2 Usage error, including a missing --jdk, or a JDK that is missing or not the version declared for it

Every commit is independently green. One change, one verification, one commit. git log on the branch is a list of verified steps.

A green build is not accepted as a green suite. Maven also succeeds when tests are skipped or missing, so build-verify adds two checks:

  • At least one test must have run, unless the project has no test sources at all.
  • If an earlier build in this run had tests and this one reports none, that is a failure (exit 3). The highest count seen is kept as a baseline and never lowered, so a regression cannot hide its own evidence.

Only test reports written by this build are counted, so stale reports from an earlier build cannot make a skipped suite look like a passing one. A partial drop in test count is a warning, not a failure, because a recipe can legitimately merge tests; the agent must judge it and record its reasoning in the change log.

Tests are never weakened to make a build pass. Adapting a test to a renamed API is repair. Changing an assertion, disabling or deleting a test, narrowing the suite, or skipping tests is not; the agent is instructed to stop and escalate instead.

What it does not guarantee: behaviour in your runtime environments, integration with other services, performance, or anything your tests do not cover.

items.title: Failure handling
items.text:
Situation Response Phase failure? Pre-flight fails Stops before creating a worktree Yes (preflight) Stage A build red Repair source and re-verify within a budget Yes, if unrepairable (java_spring_upgrade) Build exit 3 (tests did not run) Treated as red. Never fixed by skipping tests Depends on stage Test count dropped partially Agent judges and records reasoning in the change log No Stage C build red Bisect, mark offending rows failed, continue No Stage D bump red Revert that POM, mark row failed, continue No Stage E full build red Repair; no success report if unrepairable Yes, if unrepairable (final_verify)

On a phase failure the agent records error (message, step, occurred_at), leaves the worktree in place and stops. The orchestrator then retries the phase if attempts remain, or asks you to retry or abort. A retry continues from the completed stages and the worklist; it does not start over. attempt counts entries into the code phase, not individual failed builds.

items.title: Reviewing and merging the result
items.text:
Nothing is merged into your branch and nothing is pushed. Start with .modernization/modernization-summary-report.md, then inspect the branch:

git -C .modernization/code/worktree log --oneline modernization/coding-agent-<run_id>
git -C .modernization/code/worktree diff <base-ref> modernization/coding-agent-<run_id>

<base-ref> is in the summary report and in outputs.base_ref. When reviewing:

  • Stage A commit: the largest diff. Check OpenRewrite's changes and any repairs the agent made afterwards, especially to tests.
  • Stage C and D commits: one-line POM changes. Check the "Deferred and failed" section of the change log for anything that still needs a person.
  • Build report: confirm test counts stayed stable across the run.
  • Test-count warnings: read the agent's reasoning in the change log.

When satisfied, push the branch and open a pull request through your normal review process, or merge it locally. Pushing requires your confirmation; git push is never allowed automatically.

items.title: Configuration
items.text:
Variable Default Meaning MODERNIZATION_CURRENT_JAVA_VERSION 17 Java version of the JDK the project builds on today MODERNIZATION_CURRENT_JAVA_HOME /path/to/jdk-17 Home folder of that JDK. Must be set: the shipped value is a placeholder MODERNIZATION_TARGET_JAVA_VERSION 25 Default Java version offered when you are asked for the target. Also the version of the target JDK MODERNIZATION_TARGET_JAVA_HOME /path/to/jdk-25 Home folder of the target JDK. Must be set: the shipped value is a placeholder MODERNIZATION_TARGET_SPRING_BOOT_VERSION 4.1 Default Spring Boot version offered MODERNIZATION_CODING_MAX_ATTEMPTS 3 Code phase attempts before asking you to retry or abort MODERNIZATION_CODING_BUMP_BATCH_SIZE 1 Bumps applied per build verification. Larger is faster but makes a failure harder to pin down MODERNIZATION_CODING_MAX_BUMPS 0 Maximum bumps per code-phase invocation; 0 means no limit. Rows over the limit are marked deferred

The target defaults are read when the orchestrator asks you; your answer is then fixed for the run. MODERNIZATION_CODING_MAX_ATTEMPTS is copied into the phase's max_attempts when the phase first starts. Batch size and maximum bumps are read when stage D runs.

items.title: Troubleshooting
items.text: Symptom Cause Fix Pre-flight STOPPED: no executable bin/java A MODERNIZATION_*_JAVA_HOME setting still holds the placeholder, or points to the wrong folder Set it to the JDK's home folder, the one that contains bin/java (for SDKMAN, ~/.sdkman/candidates/java/<identifier>), then retry Pre-flight STOPPED: declared as Java X but runs Java Y The version setting does not match the JDK at that path Fix whichever of the pair is wrong, then retry Pre-flight: target JDK older than the chosen Java version You chose, say, Java 25 but the target JDK is 21 Point the target JDK settings at JDK 25 or newer, or choose a lower version Pre-flight: Maven runs on a different JDK than the current one ~/.mavenrc, /etc/mavenrc or MAVEN_OPTS overrides JAVA_HOME Remove that override Pre-flight: no recipe for the requested version The chosen version is not in the recipe folders (for example Spring Boot 4.0) Choose a supported version. The answer is stored for the run, so to change it run .claude/skills/orchestrator/scripts/state-set.sh .modernization/state.json gates.target_spring_boot_version=4.1, then retry Phase failed at java_spring_upgrade OpenRewrite left breakage the agent could not repair Read build-verify/stage-a/build-errors.txt and upgrade-java-spring-boot/rewrite-errors.txt; fix in the worktree or adjust targets, then retry A bump keeps failing The new version is incompatible with your code or other dependencies Expected; it is listed under "Deferred and failed" for a person to handle Stage B never finishes The inventory hang described in Known gaps Check that effective-pom and version-updates show state=SUCCESS in their logs/status files under .modernization/code/worktree/.modernization/discover/, then stop the session and resume. Successful tasks are reused, so the re-run is short Phase failed at final_verify Changes that each passed a quick build fail together Find the combination with git bisect on the branch, or retry

items.title: Determine
items.text:
The planner of the pipeline. It turns the evidence into reports, a testability score and a plan you approve before any code is touched.

Orchestrator Coordinates

  • Discover Collects
  • Determine Plans
  • Test Strengthens
  • Code Upgrades

items.title: What this is
items.text: The determine phase turns the discover phase's raw evidence into a plan. determine-agent runs three scripts at the same time: one reconciles your dependencies against the BOM catalog, available updates and known vulnerabilities; one does the same for your Maven build plugins; and one combines JaCoCo coverage and PIT mutation strength into a single testability score. The agent then reads the three reports and writes modernization-plan.md, which you approve before any code is touched.

items.title: Purpose
items.text: This phase separates "what is" from "what should change". The scripts produce facts; the agent's only judgment call is writing the plan from those facts; you review the plan before anything happens. It also produces the number that decides the next step: if your tests are too weak to trust, the pipeline strengthens them before upgrading anything.

items.title: What it does
items.text:
The agent checks that discover was approved, runs the three analysis scripts side by side, and writes the plan from their reports. After you approve the plan, the test gate picks the next phase.

flowchart TD
    V["1. Validate preconditions<br/>(discover approved, inputs present)"] --> R["2. Check for resume"]
    R --> DEP & PLG & TST
    subgraph CC["3. Concurrent analysis (one command)"]
        DEP["Dependency reconciliation"]
        PLG["Plugin reconciliation"]
        TST["Testability scoring"]
    end
    DEP & PLG & TST --> X["4. Check all three succeeded"]
    X --> SC["5. Record testability score"]
    SC --> PL["6. Write modernization-plan.md"]
    PL --> GATE{{"Approval gate"}}
    GATE -- "approved" --> TG{"7. Test gate:<br/>score ≥ threshold?"}
    TG -- "yes" --> C["Code"]
    TG -- "no" --> T["Test"]

items.title: Stage 1: Validate preconditions
items.text: The agent confirms that the discover phase is approved in .modernization/state.json and that the discover folders it needs exist: effective-pom, sbom, dependency-vulnerabilities, version-updates, bom-catalog, coverage-jacoco and coverage-pitest. A discover task that was skipped is acceptable; a missing required input stops the phase with a message naming it.

items.title: Stage 2: Check for resume
items.text: The agent reads .modernization/determine/state.json, creating it on a fresh run. The three scripts regenerate their reports from scratch each time and take seconds, so a resumed run simply runs them again.

items.title: Stage 3: Concurrent analysis
items.text: All three scripts start in a single command and run side by side. They only read discover's output and your pom.xml files, and each writes its own files, so they cannot interfere. Each script's full output goes to a log file; only a one-line status comes back to the agent.

items.title: Dependency reconciliation
items.text:
dependency-analysis/scripts/generate-dependency-report.sh reads the effective POM, the SBOM, the version updates, the vulnerability scan, the BOM catalog and your raw pom.xml files. Reading the raw files is what lets it tell "this version is managed by a BOM" apart from "this version is hard-coded".

It produces one table per module, with a row for each dependency the module declares or inherits (dependencies between your own modules are excluded):

Column Meaning Version and scope What the module uses today Inherited Whether it comes from a parent POM Latest The newest stable version available Vulnerabilities Any CVE affecting this dependency or anything it pulls in, linked to details Managed by What sets the version: the project, the parent, a BOM, or nothing

A Vulnerabilities section at the end gives each CVE's severity, CVSS score, fixed version and the dependency chain that brings it in.

Output: dependency-report.md (logs in dependency-analysis/logs/)

items.title: Plugin reconciliation
items.text:
dependency-analysis/scripts/generate-plugin-report.sh does the same for <build><plugins>: version, whether it is inherited, latest version, and what manages it (project, parent, pluginManagement, or nothing). Plugins have no vulnerability column, because they are not covered by the SBOM or the CVE scan.

Output: plugin-report.md

items.title: Testability scoring
items.text:
test-analysis/scripts/generate-testability-report.sh combines JaCoCo and PIT results for each class and for the project overall:

score = line coverage % × MODERNIZATION_JACOCO_WEIGHT
      + PIT test strength % × MODERNIZATION_PIT_WEIGHT

With the defaults that is 60% line coverage and 40% mutation strength. A class with only one of the two measurements (for example, no mutations were generated for it) is scored on the one it has. A class with neither is left out of the score.

The report contains the settings used and where they came from, an overall table (instruction, branch, line and method coverage, PIT test strength and mutation coverage, the weighted score, and whether it is above or below the threshold), a per-module summary, and the classes below the threshold, worst first.

Output: testability-report.md, testability-data.csv (every class, including excluded ones; logs in test-analysis/logs/)

items.title: Stage 4: Check all three succeeded
items.text: All three scripts are required. If any fails, the agent records which one in its state file and stops. It never writes a plan from a partial set of reports.

items.title: Stage 5: Record the testability score
items.text: The scoring script ends with the line Overall weighted testability score: NN.NN%. The agent copies that number into .modernization/determine/state.json as outputs.testability_score. The test gate reads it from there, not from the plan's text.

items.title: Stage 6: Write the plan
items.text:
The agent reads the three reports in full and writes modernization-plan.md. This is the one step in the phase that involves judgment. The plan has five sections:

Section Contents 1. Summary Links to the three reports 2. Technology stack Current Java and Spring Boot versions and other major frameworks, deduced from the reports 3. Test improvement plan If the score is below the threshold, a plan for the test phase. Otherwise, the recommended changes from the dependency and plugin reports 4. Dependency and plugin upgrades plan Whether the root POM's parent should be upgraded first; the target versions; a statement that the code phase handles the remaining upgrades and code changes 5. Modernization gains What approving the plan should achieve: CVEs resolved, dependencies and plugins brought current, end-of-life exposure removed, test improvement if the test phase runs. Quantified only where the reports support it

Section 4's target is fixed text

Section 4 always says "Java 21 and Spring Boot 4.1 or later". The plan template hard-codes this; it is not derived from your project or your settings. The versions actually applied are the ones you choose when the code phase starts (supported: Java 17, 21, 25; Spring Boot 3.5, 4.1). See Code → Target version selection.

Section 4 deliberately does not reason about individual dependencies or name OpenRewrite recipes. That work belongs to the code phase, which re-checks dependency facts after the upgrade.

The agent then marks the report step complete and sets status: reported.

Output: modernization-plan.md

items.title: Stage 7: The test gate
items.text:
After you approve the plan, the orchestrator compares the score with the threshold copied into gates.testability_threshold when the run started:

flowchart LR
    S["outputs.testability_score"] --> Q{"Score recorded and<br/>≥ threshold?"}
    Q -- "yes" --> C["Code"]
    Q -- "no, or no score" --> T["Test"]

Two details matter:

  • The comparison uses the whole-number part of the score and threshold, so a score of 79.9 against a threshold of 80 goes to the test phase.
  • If no score could be recorded, the pipeline treats it as below the threshold and runs the test phase, rather than skipping the safety net.

items.title: Outputs summary
items.text:
All paths are under .modernization/determine/.

Artifact Produced by Used by For people? modernization-plan.md Agent You, at the gate; code Yes dependency-report.md Dependency script Plan; code pre-flight Yes plugin-report.md Plugin script Plan; code pre-flight Yes testability-report.md Scoring script Plan; test phase starting point Yes testability-data.csv Scoring script Test phase (which classes to target) Readable state.json → outputs.testability_score Agent Test gate No dependency-analysis/logs/, test-analysis/logs/ Scripts You, when debugging Yes

items.title: The approval gate
items.text:
The orchestrator shows a summary of modernization-plan.md and asks you to approve or reject it. Unlike the discover report, this is the agent's interpretation, so read it critically:

  • Technology stack: does it match what you know about the project?
  • Test improvement plan: if the score is below the threshold, are the targeted areas sensible?
  • Parent POM recommendation: is upgrading the parent first appropriate for your project?
  • Gains: are they supported by the reports, or overstated?
  • Score: check it in testability-report.md alongside the per-class table. It decides whether the test phase runs.

Approve and the test gate decides the next phase.

Reject with a reason and the agent runs again with it. It decides whether your reason means an analysis is wrong (re-run the affected script, for example "this CVE is already patched") or the plan is wrong (rewrite only the plan, for example "the priorities are in the wrong order"). It prefers the narrower fix.

items.title: Configuration
items.text:
Variable Default Meaning MODERNIZATION_TESTABILITY_THRESHOLD 80 Score (%) at or above which the test phase is skipped. Also shown in testability-report.md and used to list classes below threshold MODERNIZATION_JACOCO_WEIGHT 0.6 Weight of JaCoCo line coverage, per class and overall MODERNIZATION_PIT_WEIGHT 0.4 Weight of PIT test strength, per class and overall

How these are read:

  • The scoring script reads them from the environment each time it runs. Claude Code passes the env block from settings.json to every command an agent runs.
  • The test gate uses the threshold copied into the run's state at start-up (gates.testability_threshold), not the current value in settings.json.
  • If the variables are not set at all, for example when running the script by hand outside Claude Code, the script falls back to built-in defaults (80, 0.6, 0.4). The report's "Configuration" section says which source was used.

Keep the two weights summing to 1, and change them before the run starts.

All three scripts take an optional first argument, the path to the .modernization folder. It defaults to ./.modernization, so run them from the repository root.

items.text: Symptom Cause Fix required input not found: …/coverage-jacoco/jacoco.csv (or test-strength.xml) Discover's coverage tasks produced no output, or the script was run from the wrong folder Check discover's summary.md; run scripts from the repository root or pass the path python3 (or python) is required but was not found on PATH Python missing Install Python 3; no packages needed Phase fails with a script error One of the three scripts exited non-zero Read dependency-analysis/logs/<script>.stderr.log or test-analysis/logs/testability-report.stderr.log Score looks wrong, or did not change after editing settings.json Settings not visible to the script, or changed after the run started Check the report's "Configuration" source line; see Configuration Test phase ran although the score looked close to the threshold Whole-number comparison (79.9 vs 80) Expected behaviour Determine refuses to start Discover not approved, or a required discover folder is missing Approve discover, or re-run it

items.title: Discover
items.text:
The surveyor of the pipeline. It takes a factual inventory of your build, dependencies, vulnerabilities and tests, and changes nothing.

Orchestrator Coordinates

  • Discover Collects
  • Determine Plans
  • Test Strengthens
  • Code Upgrades

items.title: What this is
items.text: The discover phase takes a factual inventory of your repository before anything is planned or changed. discover-agent runs the inventory skill, which uses Maven and a few standard tools to produce the effective POM, the dependency tree, a software bill of materials (SBOM), a list of available version updates, a vulnerability scan, JaCoCo code coverage and PIT mutation testing results. The agent then writes discover-report.md, an index of links to everything that was produced, and the pipeline stops for you to approve it. Nothing in your source code is changed.

items.title: Purpose
items.text: Every later decision depends on evidence collected here: the upgrade plan is built from the dependency and version data, and the decision to strengthen tests first comes from the coverage data. Keeping collection separate from interpretation means you can check the raw facts before anyone draws conclusions from them. Discover collects; it does not score, rank or recommend anything. That is the determine phase's job.

items.title: What it does
items.text:
The agent checks preconditions, runs the inventory skill, and turns its output into the report. Inside the skill, the read-only scans and the coverage scans run at the same time; the vulnerability scan waits only for the SBOM.

flowchart TD
    V["1. Validate preconditions<br/>(pom.xml, git)"] --> R["2. Check for resume"]

items.title: Stage 1: Validate preconditions
items.text: The agent confirms there is a pom.xml at the repository root and that git is available. If either is missing it stops with a message naming what it expected, before running anything.

items.title: Stage 2: Check for resume
items.text:
The agent reads .modernization/discover/state.json. If the file does not exist, this is a fresh run and the agent creates it with the run ID and status: running. If it exists from an earlier, interrupted session, the agent simply runs the skill again: the skill itself decides which tasks can be reused.

Resuming within the skill. Each scan task records a fingerprint of its inputs (the relevant pom.xml and source files, plus the Java, Maven and plugin versions). On a re-run, a task that succeeded before and whose fingerprint still matches is reused; anything that failed, was skipped, is missing or is out of date runs again. You can see the plan without running anything:

.claude/skills/inventory/scripts/inventory-orchestrator.sh --status

items.title: Stage 3: Preflight
items.text:
• Switches to the current JDK from .claude/settings.json (MODERNIZATION_CURRENT_JAVA_VERSION and MODERNIZATION_CURRENT_JAVA_HOME), so every scan builds your code on the JDK it builds on today. If that JDK is missing, or runs a different version than declared, discover stops and names the setting to fix.
  • Checks that either ./mvnw or mvn is available. ./mvnw is preferred when present.
  • If the repository is a git work tree, adds .modernization/ to .gitignore when that exact line is missing. If it is not a git work tree, warns that mutation testing will be skipped.
  • Copies the skill's bundled BOM catalog into .modernization/discover/bom-catalog/, replacing any previous copy.

Output: bom-catalog/ (catalog.json, catalog.yaml, bom-catalog-v1.schema.json)

The BOM catalog is reference data, not a scan result. It describes the Spring Boot dependencies BOM and the BOMs it imports. Discover does not read it; it is staged here so the determine phase can reconcile your dependencies against it.

items.title: Stage 4: Pre-warm
items.text: If any task needs to run, the skill runs mvn dependency:go-offline once, so the parallel tasks do not all download the same artifacts. If this fails, the skill carries on and each task downloads what it needs.

items.title: Stage 5: Read-only scans
items.text:
These four run in parallel and do not modify anything.

Task What it does Output effective-pom Resolves the full POM with parents and profiles applied effective-pom/effective-pom.xml dependency-tree Resolves the dependency graph dependency-tree/dependency.txt, dependency.dot sbom Generates a CycloneDX SBOM for the whole build sbom/sbom.cdx.json, sbom.cdx.xml version-updates Lists newer versions of dependencies and plugins, excluding pre-releases version-updates/dependency-updates.txt, plugin-updates.txt

effective-pom, dependency-tree and sbom are required: if any of them fails, the phase fails and no report is written. version-updates is optional.

items.title: Stage 6: Coverage scans
items.text:
These run alongside stage 5. By default each runs in its own git worktree so that they do not interfere with each other or with your checkout.

Task What it does Output coverage-jacoco Runs the test suite with JaCoCo and aggregates line, branch, instruction and method coverage coverage-jacoco/jacoco.csv, coverage-summary.txt, per-module HTML coverage-pitest Runs PIT mutation testing: introduces small code changes and checks whether the tests catch them coverage-pitest/mutations.xml, test-strength.xml

Both are optional. coverage-pitest skips itself, with the reason recorded, when:

  • the repository is not a git repository or has no commits yet;
  • the test suite does not pass (mutation testing needs a green suite to mean anything);
  • the project already configures pitest-maven itself.

These two tasks take most of the phase's time, because PIT re-runs tests for each mutation.

No score is computed here. The determine phase turns these numbers into the testability score.

items.title: Stage 7: Vulnerability scan
items.text:
Once the SBOM exists, dependency-vulnerabilities scans it for known CVEs (Common Vulnerabilities and Exposures). By default it uses grype; JFrog CLI (jf) is also supported (see Configuration).

Output: dependency-vulnerabilities/vulns.json (grype) or sbom.enriched.cdx.json (JFrog CLI)

Without a scanner the task is skipped and the report says so. Treat a skipped scan as "not assessed", not as "no vulnerabilities". The scan reflects the vulnerability database at the time it ran.

items.title: Stage 8: Summary and required-task check
items.text:
The skill writes summary.md, a table of every task with its state (including whether it was reused from a previous run) and duration. It exits with an error if any required task did not succeed. In that case the agent records the failure in its state file and stops.

Output: summary.md

items.title: Stage 9: Write the report
items.text:
The agent fills a fixed template with links to the artifacts above. It adds no commentary, ranking or scoring. Any skipped optional task appears as a one-line note in place of its link. The agent then marks the report step complete and sets status: reported.

Output: discover-report.md

items.text:
All paths are under .modernization/discover/.

Each task folder has a logs/ folder containing stdout.log, stderr.log, status (one line: state, exit code, duration), meta.json (tool versions, timing) and fingerprint.

items.title: The approval gate
items.text:
The orchestrator shows a short summary of discover-report.md and asks you to approve or reject it. Before approving, open the report and check:

  • Every scan you expect actually ran. Skipped tasks are listed in place of their links, with the reason. A skipped coverage task means the testability score will be based on less data.
  • The vulnerability scan ran, or you accept that it was not assessed.
  • summary.md shows no failures and plausible durations.

Approve and the run moves to the determine phase.

Reject with a reason and the agent runs again with your reason. It decides whether the reason means the data is wrong (re-run specific tasks with --only, or everything with --force) or the report itself is wrong (rewrite it from the existing data). It prefers the narrower fix unless your reason clearly says the data is wrong, so be specific: "the dependency tree is missing module X" leads to a re-scan, "the report links are broken" leads to a rewrite.

items.title: Configuration
items.text:
The discover phase builds on the current JDK (MODERNIZATION_CURRENT_JAVA_VERSION and MODERNIZATION_CURRENT_JAVA_HOME, see Code). Apart from that, it has no settings of its own in settings.json. The three testability settings are copied into the run's state when it starts, but they are used by the determine phase:

Variable Default Meaning Effect in discover MODERNIZATION_TESTABILITY_THRESHOLD 80 Score needed to skip the test phase Copied to gates.testability_threshold at run start MODERNIZATION_JACOCO_WEIGHT 0.6 Weight of line coverage in the score Copied to gates.testability_weights.jacoco MODERNIZATION_PIT_WEIGHT 0.4 Weight of mutation strength in the score Copied to gates.testability_weights.pit

Advanced settings. The inventory skill reads these environment variables. They are not in settings.json by default; add them to its env block to change them.

Variable Default Meaning VULN_SCANNER grype Vulnerability scanner: grype or jf (JFrog CLI) TASK_TIMEOUT_DEFAULT 1800 Timeout in seconds for each scan task except PIT TASK_TIMEOUT_PITEST 3600 Timeout in seconds for PIT mutation testing COVERAGE_ISOLATION worktree worktree runs the coverage tasks in parallel, each in its own git worktree; serial runs them one after the other in your checkout MVN ./mvnw if present, else mvn Maven command to use

Skill options. When running the skill by hand, or when the agent re-runs it after a rejection:

Option Effect (none) Resume: re-run failed, skipped, missing or out-of-date tasks, reuse the rest --force Run every task, ignoring previous results --only t1,t2 Run only these tasks, plus any they depend on --ignore-staleness Reuse any previous success without checking fingerprints --status Print the resume plan and exit

items.title: Troubleshooting
items.text:
Symptom Cause Fix required task 'X' is not SUCCESS effective-pom, dependency-tree or sbom failed, usually a Maven build or resolution problem Read .modernization/discover/<task>/logs/stderr.log, fix the cause, then resume Coverage tasks fail with "no POM in this directory" or worktree errors The project is not its own git repository Run git init at the project root and resume; only the failed tasks re-run coverage-pitest skipped: "requires a green suite" The test suite fails Fix the failing tests and resume coverage-pitest skipped: "already configures pitest-maven" Your POM already declares the PIT plugin Known limitation; the score will use JaCoCo only coverage-pitest skipped: "git worktree add failed" The repository has no commits yet Make an initial commit and resume dependency-vulnerabilities skipped: "grype not installed" No scanner Install grype, or set VULN_SCANNER=jf with JFrog CLI installed A task times out Large project or slow network Raise TASK_TIMEOUT_DEFAULT or TASK_TIMEOUT_PITEST in the env block A task you expected to re-run was reused Its inputs have not changed Use --only <task> or --force (or reject with a reason saying the data is stale)

Do not edit files under .modernization/discover/<task>/ by hand. Re-run the task instead, so the recorded state and fingerprints stay consistent.

items.title: Orchestrator
items.text:
The conductor of the pipeline. It sequences the phases, remembers where a run is, and asks you before anything moves forward.

Orchestrator Coordinates

  • Discover Collects
  • Determine Plans
  • Test Strengthens
  • Code Upgrades

items.title: What it is
items.text:
The orchestrator is not a subagent. It is the main Claude Code session itself, driven by the project's CLAUDE.md. It invokes one phase agent at a time, waits for it to finish, then decides what happens next.

Its work splits into two halves, and each half lives in a different place:

Bookkeeping

Lives in the orchestrator skill

  • Read and write state.json
  • Decide the next state transition
  • Compare a score with a threshold

Scripts only. No judgment.

Judgment

Lives in CLAUDE.md

  • Invoke a phase agent with the right prompt
  • Summarise a report for you
  • Ask you to approve or reject, and react to it

The main session's own reasoning.

Neither half can replace the other. A skill cannot invoke a subagent or ask you a question. And state transitions should not be re-derived from prose every turn, where they can drift, so they are encoded once as a lookup table in a read-only script.

  • One phase at a time

    Phase agents run synchronously. Nothing to poll, no two phases ever overlap.

  • State lives in files

    Every decision and invocation is recorded under .modernization/. Stop, resume, audit.

  • Agents stay isolated

    Each agent starts with a clean context and a short prompt. It reads the rest itself.

items.title: The pipeline
items.text:
The orchestrator's flow

flowchart TD
    OA(["orchestrator"])
    OA -->|" 1. calls "| DA["discover-agent"]
    DA -->|" produces "| DR[("discover-report.md")]
    DR -->|" reviewed by "| OA
    OA -.->|" rejected → revise "| DA
    OA -->|" 2. approved → calls "| DETA["determine-agent"]
    DETA -->|" produces "| DETR[("modernization-plan.md")]
    DETR -->|" reviewed by "| OA
    OA -.->|" rejected → revise "| DETA
    OA -->|" 3. score < threshold → calls "| TA["test-agent"]
    TA -->|" produces "| TR[("tests + testability-report.md")]
    TR -->|" reviewed by "| OA
    OA -.->|" rejected → revise "| TA
    OA -->|" 4. score ≥ threshold, or test approved → calls "| CA["coding-agent"]
    CA -->|" once the build passes "| MP[("upgrade + modernization-summary-report.md")]

You approve each phase's report before the next one starts. Test runs only when the testability score is below the threshold. Code ends with a branch ready for your review.

items.title: Checkpoints
items.text:
Mechanical checks

Decided from a number, without asking

  • Test gate Score ≥ threshold → Code, else → Test
  • Build verification Build and tests pass → Done, else retry, then ask you

Human gates

You approve, or reject with a reason

  • discover-report.md Rejected → Discover re-runs
  • modernization-plan.md Rejected → Determine re-runs
  • testability-report.md Rejected → Test continues

Why the code phase has no approval gate

Its changes are judged by whether the build and tests pass. The human review happens when you inspect and merge its branch.

items.title: Building blocks
items.text:
• Orchestrator prompt

    Runs the turn loop, invokes agents, asks you questions.

    CLAUDE.md

  • Orchestrator skill

    Creates, reads and updates state files. Decides the next step.

    .claude/skills/orchestrator/

  • Phase agents

    One specialist per phase, each with its own context and tools.

    .claude/agents/<phase>-agent.md

  • Skills

    Reusable procedures the agents call: scripts plus instructions.

    .claude/skills/<name>/

  • Settings

    Tool permissions and pipeline configuration.

    .claude/settings.json

  • State and artifacts

    State files, reports, logs and worktrees, created at run time.

    .modernization/

Agent Skills it uses discover-agent inventory determine-agent dependency-analysis, test-analysis test-agent testability coding-agent upgrade-java-spring-boot, build-verify, dependency-upgrade

Every agent also uses the orchestrator skill to read and write its own state file.

Related, not interchangeable

  • A skill knows how to do one job, not when to run.
  • An agent applies skills within its phase, but cannot move the pipeline or ask you anything.
  • Only the orchestrator sequences phases and talks to you.

items.title: Who does what
items.text:
• Scripts Everything deterministic

    Run Maven, generate the SBOM, compute coverage, edit pom.xml, verify a build.

  • Agents Everything that needs judgment

    Write the plan, pick classes to test, write tests, repair code after OpenRewrite.

  • Orchestrator Sequencing

    Read state, ask a script what is next, invoke an agent or ask you.

  • You Decisions

    Approve or reject reports, choose target versions, review and merge.

Scripts write full output to log files and return a single status line. Agents read finished summaries, never raw build output, so their context stays small.

items.title: How a turn works
items.text:
sequenceDiagram
    actor You
    participant O as Orchestrator (CLAUDE.md)
    participant T as orchestrator-turn.sh
    participant A as Phase agent
    participant S as .modernization/

    You->>O: "Start the modernization pipeline."
    O->>S: state-init.sh (first run only)
    loop until DONE or stopped
        O->>T: What next?
        T->>S: read current_state (+ score or attempts)
        T-->>O: one action
        alt RUN_AGENT
            O->>S: set phase to RUNNING
            O->>A: invoke (with rejection reason or retry context)
            A->>S: write artifacts and phase state.json
            A-->>O: short conclusion
            O->>S: append session record, set next state
        else AWAIT_APPROVAL
            O->>You: report summary: approve or reject?
            You-->>O: decision (+ reason if rejected)
            O->>S: record decision, set next state
        else AWAIT_MITIGATION
            O->>You: the error: retry or abort?
        end
    end

orchestrator-turn.sh is read-only and returns exactly one of four actions:

Action The orchestrator then… RUN_AGENT Invokes the next phase agent and records the session. Before the first coding-agent run, it asks you for the target versions AWAIT_APPROVAL Summarises the report and asks you to approve or reject AWAIT_MITIGATION Shows the error and asks you to retry or abort DONE Reports the final summary and stops

The state machine is a lookup table, so the running pipeline cannot drift from the designed flow.

items.title: Configuration
items.text:
All configuration lives in .claude/settings.json, in two blocks:

Env

Pipeline settings, passed as environment variables to every command the agents run.

Permissions

Which commands and files the agents may use without asking.

items.title: Pipeline settings
items.text:
Variable Default Phase Meaning MODERNIZATION_TESTABILITY_THRESHOLD 80 Determine, Test Score (%) needed to skip Test, and the target Test works toward MODERNIZATION_JACOCO_WEIGHT 0.6 Determine, Test Weight of JaCoCo line coverage MODERNIZATION_PIT_WEIGHT 0.4 Determine, Test Weight of PIT mutation strength MODERNIZATION_TEST_MAX_ITERATIONS 5 Test Max write-tests-and-re-measure rounds MODERNIZATION_CODING_MAX_ATTEMPTS 3 Code Attempts before asking you to retry or abort MODERNIZATION_CURRENT_JAVA_VERSION 17 All Java version of the JDK your project builds on today MODERNIZATION_CURRENT_JAVA_HOME placeholder All Home folder of that JDK. You must set it MODERNIZATION_TARGET_JAVA_VERSION 25 Code Default Java version offered (supported: 17, 21, 25), and the version of the target JDK MODERNIZATION_TARGET_JAVA_HOME placeholder Code Home folder of the target JDK. You must set it MODERNIZATION_TARGET_SPRING_BOOT_VERSION 4.1 Code Default Spring Boot version offered (supported: 3.5, 4.1) MODERNIZATION_CODING_BUMP_BATCH_SIZE 1 Code Dependency bumps per build verification MODERNIZATION_CODING_MAX_BUMPS 0 Code Max bumps per invocation (0 = no limit)

Testability score

line coverage % × JaCoCo weight + PIT strength % × PIT weight

Keep the two weights summing to 1.

Two JDKs, switched automatically

Everything that builds your code as it is today (discover, test, and the OpenRewrite migration) runs on the current JDK. Every build after the migration runs on the target JDK. Each script sets JAVA_HOME for its own run only, from these settings. If a home folder has no bin/java, or runs a different version than declared, the script stops and names the setting to fix. The code phase's pre-flight checks both JDKs before anything else. The orchestrator records the current version as gates.current_java_version next to the target.

Discover also accepts a few advanced variables (scanner choice, task timeouts). See Discover.

Target versions: the plan's text is not what gets applied

modernization-plan.md always says "Java 21 and Spring Boot 4.1 or later": that wording is fixed in the plan template. The versions actually applied are the ones you choose when the code phase starts. Supported targets are Java 17, 21, 25 and Spring Boot 3.5, 4.1. There is no Spring Boot 4.1 recipe yet, so pre-flight rejects it.

items.title: Permissions
items.text:
Allowed without asking

  • The pipeline's own scripts under .claude/skills/*/scripts/
  • mvn, ./mvnw, mvn -v, java -version
  • Read-only git: status, branch, diff, log, worktree
  • Commits and resets only inside the pipeline's worktrees (git -C .modernization/test/worktree …, git -C .modernization/code/worktree …)
  • Anything under .modernization/
  • Basic shell: ls, cat, find, head, tail, wc, echo, pwd, cp, mkdir -p .modernization/**

Always asks first

git push, and git commit or git reset on your own branch.

Always denied

.env, any *.pem file, and anything under secrets/.

Least privilege: agents build, test and commit freely inside their own worktrees, and nowhere else.

Extending the pipeline with a new script? Add its exact path to allow, rather than broadening an existing pattern.

items.title: Changing configuration safely
items.text:
Edit settings.json before you start a run

  • At run start, state-init.sh snapshots the threshold, weights and caps into gates in .modernization/state.json.
  • The test gate uses that snapshot, so a mid-run change won't alter a plan you already approved. Some scripts read the environment directly (weights, batch size), so mid-run edits apply unevenly. Avoid them.
  • Score looks wrong? Check the testability report's Configuration section. "Built-in default" where you expected your own values means the script ran outside a Claude Code session.

items.title: State
items.text:
The pipeline's memory lives in files, not in the chat. Close the session any time, resume later, and see exactly what happened.

Each phase records which steps it has finished. The orchestrator records which phase the run is in and what you have approved.

items.title: Where state lives
items.text:
.modernization/
├── state.json                      Top-level run state (orchestrator)
├── discover/
│   ├── state.json                  Discover step progress

► marks the files written for people. Everything else is machine state, intermediate data or logs.

One change outside .modernization/

On its first run inside a git repository, Discover adds .modernization/ to your .gitignore if it is missing. You will see it as an uncommitted edit.

items.title: The state machine
items.text:
stateDiagram-v2
    [*] --> INIT
    INIT --> DISCOVER_RUNNING
    DISCOVER_RUNNING --> DISCOVER_AWAITING_APPROVAL: report written
    DISCOVER_AWAITING_APPROVAL --> DETERMINE_RUNNING: approved
    DISCOVER_AWAITING_APPROVAL --> DISCOVER_RUNNING: rejected
    DETERMINE_RUNNING --> DETERMINE_AWAITING_APPROVAL: plan written
    DETERMINE_AWAITING_APPROVAL --> TEST_GATE_CHECK: approved
    DETERMINE_AWAITING_APPROVAL --> DETERMINE_RUNNING: rejected
    TEST_GATE_CHECK --> CODING_RUNNING: score ≥ threshold
    TEST_GATE_CHECK --> TEST_RUNNING: score below threshold
    TEST_RUNNING --> TEST_AWAITING_APPROVAL: threshold reached or cap hit
    TEST_AWAITING_APPROVAL --> CODING_RUNNING: approved
    TEST_AWAITING_APPROVAL --> TEST_RUNNING: rejected
    CODING_RUNNING --> DONE: build green
    CODING_RUNNING --> CODING_RUNNING: failed, attempts left
    CODING_RUNNING --> ASK: failed, no attempts left
    DISCOVER_RUNNING --> FAILED: phase failed
    DETERMINE_RUNNING --> FAILED: phase failed
    TEST_RUNNING --> FAILED: phase failed
    FAILED --> ASK
    state "You choose: retry or abort" as ASK
    ASK --> RETRY: retry
    state "Failed phase runs again (PHASE_RUNNING)" as RETRY
    ASK --> [*]: abort
    DONE --> [*]
State Meaning INIT Run created, nothing started <PHASE>_RUNNING The phase's agent is working, or runs next turn <PHASE>_AWAITING_APPROVAL Waiting for your decision. Not stuck TEST_GATE_CHECK Next turn compares the score with the threshold FAILED Discover, determine or test failed. You are asked to retry or abort DONE Green build. Branch ready for review

A failing code phase never enters FAILED. It stays in CODING_RUNNING and retries; once its attempts are used up you are asked to retry or abort. Choosing retry grants one more attempt. Abort just stops the session; the state is kept, so a later session asks you again.

Not every stop is a failure

  • A test phase that hits its iteration cap still writes a report and waits for your approval.
  • A failing code phase retries on its own up to MODERNIZATION_CODING_MAX_ATTEMPTS before asking you.

items.title: Who writes what
items.text:
File Field Written by .modernization/state.json Everything Orchestrator only .modernization/<phase>/state.json status, steps, outputs, error, attempt, max_attempts That phase's agent .modernization/<phase>/state.json sessions Orchestrator, after every invocation

All writes go through state-set.sh or state-append-session.sh: write to a temp file, then rename. A killed process can never leave a half-written state file.

Key fields reference File Field What it tells you state.json run_id Unique ID for this run, also used in branch names state.json current_state Where the run is in the state machine state.json phases.<phase>.status pending, running, awaiting_approval, approved, rejected, failed or remediating (retrying after a failure). Also skipped for test, completed for code state.json phases.<phase>.rejection_reason Your reason, passed to the agent when it re-runs. Cleared on approval state.json gates.* Settings snapshotted at run start, plus your chosen target versions <phase>/state.json status running, reported, completed or failed <phase>/state.json steps Which steps are done. This makes resume step-level <phase>/state.json error {message, step, occurred_at} when the phase failed <phase>/state.json sessions One entry per invocation: session ID, start, end, transcript determine/state.json outputs.testability_score The number the test gate compares

Phases are named discover, determine, test and code in state files and directories.

To watch these during a run, see monitoring.

  • Discover

    Collects a factual inventory of dependencies, versions, vulnerabilities and test coverage. Changes nothing.

  • Determine

    Plans the upgrade from that evidence, and scores whether your tests are strong enough to trust it.

  • Test

    Strengthens weak tests, round by round on its own branch, before anything is upgraded.

  • Code

    Upgrades Java, Spring Boot and dependencies, one verified commit at a time.

items.title: Quick Start
items.text: From zero to your first modernization run in four steps.

items.title: Before you start
items.text:
• A Maven project

    pom.xml at the root. Single- or multi-module.

  • Its own git repo

    .git next to pom.xml. If not, run git init.

  • A passing build

    ./mvnw clean install succeeds today.

Run every command below from your project root.

What happens next

The pipeline pauses for your approval after each phase and asks which Java and Spring Boot versions to target. Nothing is committed to your branch. The upgrade lands on its own modernization/* branch for you to review and merge. See About for how it works.

items.title: Check prerequisites
items.text:
Check Install missing 
curl -fsSL https://cortexaidevkit.org/pages/modernize/quick-start/check-prereqs.sh | bash

curl -fsSL https://cortexaidevkit.org/pages/modernize/quick-start/check-prereqs.sh | bash -s -- --install

You're set when it prints Ready.

What the script checks Item Why claude Runs the pipeline git Isolates builds and changes in worktrees java and mvn (or ./mvnw) Builds your project jq Reads the pipeline's state files python3 Writes the reports, scores tests and edits pom.xml (determine, test and code phases) bash Runs the pipeline's scripts grype (optional) Vulnerability scan. Skipped without it pom.xml and .git The project is Maven, in its own git repository

--install uses Homebrew on macOS, or apt / dnf on Linux. It installs JDK 21 if no JDK is found. To pick another, end the command with | JDK_VERSION=25 bash -s -- --install.

You need two JDKs installed: the one your project builds on today and the one you upgrade to. They can be the same. The script prints the Java version your pom.xml declares. Once the pipeline is added, re-run the script to check both JDKs.

items.title: Add the agent to your project
items.text:
curl -fsSL https://github.com/CortexAIDevKit/java-springboot-modernize-claude-agent/archive/main.tar.gz \
  | tar -xz --strip-components=2 \
      java-springboot-modernize-claude-agent-main/final/CLAUDE.md \
      java-springboot-modernize-claude-agent-main/final/.claude

This adds CLAUDE.md and .claude/ to your project.

Already have a CLAUDE.md or .claude/?

They will be overwritten. Back them up first, then merge your settings back into .claude/settings.json.

items.title: Set your two JDKs
items.text:
The pipeline builds your current code on the current JDK, and the upgraded code on the target JDK. It switches between them itself. Set both in the env block of .claude/settings.json. The shipped paths are placeholders, so the pipeline stops until you set them.

"MODERNIZATION_CURRENT_JAVA_VERSION": "17",
"MODERNIZATION_CURRENT_JAVA_HOME": "/Users/you/.sdkman/candidates/java/17.0.19-tem",
"MODERNIZATION_TARGET_JAVA_VERSION": "25",
"MODERNIZATION_TARGET_JAVA_HOME": "/Users/you/.sdkman/candidates/java/25.0.3-tem"

Use the folder that contains bin/java. On macOS, /usr/libexec/java_home -v 17 prints it. Each version must match the JDK at its path, or the pipeline stops and names the mismatch. To keep machine-specific paths out of git, put these four keys in .claude/settings.local.json instead.

Re-run the prerequisite script. It checks both JDKs.

Optional: change the defaults

Edit the env block in .claude/settings.json before you start:

  • MODERNIZATION_TESTABILITY_THRESHOLD (default 80): below this score, the test phase runs.
  • MODERNIZATION_TARGET_JAVA_VERSION (default 25) and MODERNIZATION_TARGET_SPRING_BOOT_VERSION (default 4.1): the targets offered to you. Supported: Java 17, 21, 25; Spring Boot 3.5, 4.1.

items.title: Start the pipeline
items.text:
claude

If Claude Code asks whether you trust this folder, accept. Otherwise it ignores .claude/settings.json and every pipeline script stops to ask for approval.

Then type:

Start the modernization pipeline

items.title: Test
items.text:
The safety net of the pipeline. It writes tests in rounds, on its own branch, to raise the testability score before anything is upgraded.

Orchestrator Coordinates

  • Discover Collects
  • Determine Plans
  • Test Strengthens
  • Code Upgrades

items.title: What this is
items.text: The test phase runs only when the determine phase's testability score is below the threshold. test-agent writes new JUnit tests, or extends existing ones, in a separate git worktree on its own branch. After each round it re-measures JaCoCo coverage and PIT mutation strength, commits that round's tests, and repeats until the score reaches the threshold or it has used its allowed number of rounds. It then writes testability-report.md and the pipeline stops for you to approve it.

items.title: Purpose
items.text: An upgrade is only as trustworthy as the tests that check it. If the existing tests would miss regressions, the code phase's "the build is green" signal means little. This phase raises the safety net before any production code changes, and leaves every round of new tests as a separate commit you can review. Coverage and mutation strength are proxies for test quality, not proof of it, which is why you review the tests before approving.

items.title: At a glance
items.text:
flowchart LR

        direction TB
        IN("<b>↓ INPUTS</b><br/><br/>Approved modernization-plan.md<br/>testability-report.md<br/>testability-data.csv<br/>Your repository")
        AG(["<b>test-agent</b>"])
        OUT("<b>↑ OUTPUTS</b><br/><br/>Test branch, one commit per round<br/>testability-report.md<br/>Measurements per round")
        IN -- reads --> AG -- writes --> OUT
    end

    DT(["② determine-agent"]) == "score < threshold" ==> TEST
    TEST ==> C(["④ coding-agent"])

    classDef agent fill:#3b82f633,stroke:#3b82f6,stroke-width:2.5px
    classDef io fill:#3b82f60d,stroke:#60a5fa80,stroke-width:1px
    classDef other fill:transparent,stroke:#94a3b880,stroke-width:1px,stroke-dasharray:4 4

Agent test-agent Skills testability (plus orchestrator for state) Runs when The test gate finds the score below MODERNIZATION_TESTABILITY_THRESHOLD, or no score was recorded Inputs Approved modernization-plan.md, testability-report.md and testability-data.csv from determine; your repository Outputs Branch modernization/test-agent-<run_id> with one commit per round; .modernization/test/testability-report.md; measurements per round Human gate Yes: approve or reject testability-report.md Next phase Code (on approve); test again with your reason (on reject) Changes to your repository Test code, and test-scoped dependencies in pom.xml, only inside .modernization/test/worktree. Your checked-out branch is not touched

items.title: What it does
items.text:
The agent sets up a separate worktree, then writes tests in rounds. Each round targets the weakest classes, re-measures the score and commits. Rounds stop when the score reaches the threshold or the allowed number of rounds is used up.

flowchart TD
    V["1. Validate preconditions"] --> R["2. Resume or create worktree"]
    R --> SP["3. Read starting point"]
    SP --> PK
    subgraph LOOP["4. One round (repeats)"]
        PK["4a. Pick classes to target"] --> WR["4b. Write or extend tests"]
        WR --> ME["4c. Re-measure coverage and score"]
        ME --> ST["4d. Stage, check scope, commit"]
        ST --> UP["4e. Record the round"]
    end
    UP --> CK{"4f. Score ≥ threshold<br/>or rounds used up?"}
    CK -- "no" --> PK
    CK -- "yes" --> REP["5. Write testability-report.md"]
    REP --> GATE{{"Approval gate"}}

items.title: Stage 1: Validate preconditions
items.text: The agent confirms the run is in TEST_RUNNING (it never re-decides the test gate itself), that the determine phase's plan, testability report and per-class data exist, and that the repository is a git work tree. Git is required here, not optional. If anything is missing it stops before creating a worktree.

items.title: Stage 2: Resume or create the worktree
items.text:
On a fresh run the agent creates .modernization/test/state.json, with attempt set to 0 and max_attempts taken from the run's gates.test_max_iterations (copied from MODERNIZATION_TEST_MAX_ITERATIONS at run start, default 5). It then creates the worktree:

git worktree add .modernization/test/worktree -b modernization/test-agent-<run_id> HEAD

All test-writing happens in this worktree. Because .modernization/ is in .gitignore, the worktree does not show up in your normal git status.

If the worktree already exists, from an interrupted session or after you rejected the report, the agent reuses it and continues from the recorded attempt. It never recreates the worktree or discards earlier commits.

Output: worktree and branch modernization/test-agent-<run_id>

items.title: Stage 3: Read the starting point
items.text: The agent reads determine's testability-report.md (the score before any new tests) and testability-data.csv (every class, worst first). The final report links back to this starting point.

items.title: Stage 4: Rounds of test-writing
items.text: Each round increases attempt by one and then:

items.title: 4a. Pick classes to target
items.text: From the latest per-class data (determine's on the first round, the previous round's measurement after that), the agent picks a batch of classes below the threshold where a modest number of tests would raise the score most. Batch size is the agent's judgment: large enough to make progress, small enough that the next measurement gives useful feedback.

items.title: 4b. Write or extend tests
items.text:
The agent writes or extends JUnit tests under src/test/java in the worktree. This is the phase's main judgment step. It may add a test-scoped dependency to a pom.xml, such as a mocking library if the project has none. It never changes production code under src/main, never adds a production dependency, and never touches <dependencyManagement>.

Output: new or changed test files

items.title: 4c. Re-measure
items.text:
.claude/skills/testability/scripts/measure-testability.sh \
  .modernization/test/worktree .modernization/test/iterations/<attempt>

This runs a real Maven build on the current JDK (the code is not upgraded yet) with JaCoCo, then PIT mutation testing in a separate temporary copy (so the PIT plugin added for measurement never ends up in the pom.xml that gets committed), and scores the result with the same formula as the determine phase. It is a full measurement every time, not a cached one, so each round takes about as long as discover's coverage scans.

A non-zero exit here means the build or the test suite failed, not that the score is low. See Failure handling.

Output: .modernization/test/iterations/<n>/ containing coverage-jacoco/, coverage-pitest/, testability-report.md and testability-data.csv

items.title: 4d. Stage, check scope, commit
items.text:
git -C .modernization/test/worktree add -A -- . ':!**/target' ':!**/target/**'
.claude/skills/testability/scripts/check-scope.sh .modernization/test/worktree <previous-commit>
git -C .modernization/test/worktree commit -m "<header>" -m "<body>"
  • Build output under target/ is always excluded, even if your project's .gitignore does not exclude it.
  • check-scope.sh checks the staged changes and fails, naming each file, if anything outside src/test/** or a pom.xml changed. On failure the agent unstages, fixes the change and tries again within the same round. A failing scope check is never committed.
  • Commits use Conventional Commits, with the round and score change in the body:
test(testability): raise coverage on OrderService, PricingEngine

Iteration 2/5 of automated test remediation (test-agent).
Weighted testability score: 71.20% -> 76.85% (threshold: 80%)

The agent is allowed to commit only with git -C .modernization/test/worktree commit. A plain git commit anywhere else would ask you first.

Output: one commit on the test branch

items.title: 4e. Record the round
items.text: The agent updates its state file: attempt, the latest outputs.testability_score, and an entry in steps.iterations with the classes targeted, score before and after, and the commit SHA.

items.title: 4f. Check whether to stop
items.text:
• Score at or above the threshold: stop, with outputs.threshold_reached: true.
  • All rounds used and still below: stop, with outputs.threshold_reached: false. This is not a failure: the agent still writes a report and you decide whether the improvement is enough.
  • Otherwise: start the next round.

items.title: Stage 5: Write the report
items.text:
Output: .modernization/test/testability-report.md, with these sections:

Section Contents Starting point Link to determine's testability report, and the starting score and threshold Remediation summary How many rounds ran, the final score, whether the threshold was reached, which classes were targeted Iteration history One row per round: classes targeted, score before, score after, commit Where to see the changes The worktree path, branch name, and the git log and git diff commands to inspect the tests Outcome "Reached threshold after N iterations", or that the iteration cap was reached below the threshold

The agent then marks the report step complete and sets status: reported.

items.title: Outputs summary
items.text: Artifact Path For people? Report .modernization/test/testability-report.md Yes New tests, one commit per round Branch modernization/test-agent-<run_id> in .modernization/test/worktree/ Yes Measurement per round .modernization/test/iterations/<n>/ When debugging State, including iteration history .modernization/test/state.json Readable

items.title: Failure handling
items.text: Situation What happens Re-measurement fails (build breaks or tests fail) Phase failure. The agent records error with step: iteration_<n> and stops. The worktree and earlier commits are kept for debugging or a retry Scope check fails Not a phase failure. Fixed and retried within the round; escalated only if no in-scope change can be produced Iteration cap reached below threshold Not a failure. Report written, waits for your approval Preconditions missing Stops before creating or touching a worktree

items.title: The approval gate
items.text:
The orchestrator shows a summary of testability-report.md and asks you to approve or reject it. Before approving:

  • Read the tests, not just the score. Inspect them on the branch:
git -C .modernization/test/worktree log --oneline modernization/test-agent-<run_id>
git -C .modernization/test/worktree diff <base-commit> modernization/test-agent-<run_id>

Look for tests that assert real behaviour, rather than tests that only execute code to raise coverage. - Check the outcome. Did the score reach the threshold, or did the agent run out of rounds?

Approve and the run moves to the code phase, with whatever improvement was made.

Reject with a reason and the agent continues from where it stopped, with your reason as guidance. Earlier commits are kept; a rejection here usually means "keep going", not "start over".

If the iteration cap was reached, rejecting does not give the agent more rounds: the cap counts every round across the whole phase, including rounds after a rejection. The agent will report that no rounds remain and name the setting to raise. Your options are to approve and proceed with the partial improvement, or to raise MODERNIZATION_TEST_MAX_ITERATIONS and start a fresh run, because the cap for this run was fixed when it started.

Approving does not merge the branch. To keep the new tests in your own branch regardless of what the code phase does, merge or cherry-pick them yourself, or push the branch and open a pull request:

git merge modernization/test-agent-<run_id>

items.title: Configuration

Copied to gates.test_max_iterations at run start, then into this phase's max_attempts MODERNIZATION_TESTABILITY_THRESHOLD 80 The score the phase works toward MODERNIZATION_JACOCO_WEIGHT 0.6 Line coverage weight used when re-measuring MODERNIZATION_PIT_WEIGHT 0.4 Mutation strength weight used when re-measuring

The iteration cap is fixed when the run starts. Changing settings.json during a run does not change it.

items.text: Symptom Cause Fix required input not found, or determine artifacts missing Determine not approved, or session started from the wrong folder Start the session from the repository root Phase failed at iteration_<n> The build or test suite failed during re-measurement Look in .modernization/test/iterations/<n>/ and the worktree; fix, then retry from the failure prompt A round's changes look wrong The agent's tests need correcting Every round is a separate commit; inspect with git -C .modernization/test/worktree log -p. Nothing is squashed Score barely moves despite new tests Remaining PIT gaps may be equivalent mutants: code changes that no test could detect because behaviour does not change Check the report's remediation summary; approve if the remaining gap is not real test weakness Iteration cap reached repeatedly The cap counts all rounds in the phase Approve, or raise the setting and start a fresh run
